sub_graphs.title: DAS Core: Custody Group Assignment and Column Distribution
sub_graphs.description: Models how nodes are deterministically assigned custody groups and corresponding columns, including subnet joining and data availability obligations

nodes.label: Node Without Custody Assignment
nodes.description: A node has joined the network but has not yet computed its custody group assignments

nodes.label: Compute Custody Groups via get_custody_groups
nodes.description: Deterministically compute custody group indices from node_id using pseudo-random selection with iteration, ensuring at least CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) groups

nodes.label: Custody Groups Assigned
nodes.description: Node has computed its set of custody group indices (minimum 4, up to custody_group_count advertised in ENR)

nodes.label: Compute Columns for Custody Groups
nodes.description: Map each custody group to column indices using formula: NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group, yielding specific columns the node must custody

nodes.label: Custody Columns Determined
nodes.description: Node knows which of the 128 columns it is responsible for storing and serving

nodes.label: Join Gossip Subnets for Custody Groups
nodes.description: Node subscribes to gossip subnets corresponding to its assigned custody groups to receive column data

nodes.label: Subscribed to Column Subnets
nodes.description: Node is actively receiving column gossip on subnets for its custody groups

edges.label: Column indices computed via NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group

external_entities.name: Network Peers
external_entities.description: Other nodes that can verify custody obligations using the deterministic public assignment function and request columns via Req/Resp

external_entities.name: Peer Node
external_entities.description: Any peer that can verify a node's custody obligations using the public deterministic assignment function

sub_graphs.title: DAS Core: Data Availability Sampling Per Slot
sub_graphs.description: Models the per-slot sampling process where nodes verify data availability by sampling custody groups and validating column data

nodes.label: New Slot Begins
nodes.description: A new slot has started and the node must perform data availability sampling

nodes.label: Determine Sample Set
nodes.description: Select max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count) groups to sample for this slot; actual custody groups are a subset of sampled groups

nodes.label: Sample Set Determined
nodes.description: The set of custody groups to sample this slot is known (at least 8 groups)

nodes.label: Collect Columns via Gossip
nodes.description: Receive column data from subscribed gossip subnets for sampled groups

nodes.label: Request Missing Columns via Req/Resp
nodes.description: For columns not received via gossip, request them from peers using Req/Resp protocol

nodes.label: Sampled Columns Collected
nodes.description: Column data for sampled groups has been gathered from gossip and/or Req/Resp

nodes.label: Verify KZG Proofs for Column Cells
nodes.description: Validate KZG proofs in DataColumnSidecar against KZG commitments to ensure column data integrity

nodes.label: Data Availability Confirmed
nodes.description: All sampled columns have valid KZG proofs; data is considered available for this slot

nodes.label: Data Availability Sampling Failed
nodes.description: One or more sampled columns could not be obtained or had invalid proofs; data availability not confirmed

edges.label: Listen for columns on subscribed subnets
Proof verification failed or columns missing
edges.condition: Proof verification failed or columns missing

external_entities.name: Gossip Network
external_entities.description: P2P gossip layer delivering DataColumnSidecars on per-custody-group subnets

external_entities.name: Req/Resp Peers
external_entities.description: Peers that respond to direct column data requests when gossip delivery is incomplete

sub_graphs.title: DAS Core: Matrix Reconstruction and Cross-Seeding
sub_graphs.description: Models the erasure coding reconstruction of the full data matrix from partial columns and subsequent re-gossip of recovered data

nodes.label: Partial Matrix Available
nodes.description: Node has received more than 50% of columns (at least 65 of 128) for the current block

nodes.label: Recover Full Matrix via Erasure Coding
nodes.description: Use recover_matrix function to reconstruct all 128 columns from the 50%+ columns available, using one-dimensional erasure coding

nodes.label: Full Matrix Recovered
nodes.description: All columns have been reconstructed from partial data

nodes.label: Expose Reconstructed Columns as Received Data
nodes.description: Make reconstructed columns available as if they were received from the network, enabling other subsystems to access them

nodes.label: Re-Gossip Reconstructed Columns on Subscribed Subnets
nodes.description: Forward reconstructed columns on subnets the node is subscribed to, cross-seeding data to peers

nodes.label: Reconstructed Columns Distributed
nodes.description: Reconstructed column data has been re-gossiped to the network

external_entities.name: Subnet Peers
external_entities.description: Peers on subnets the node is subscribed to, who receive re-gossiped reconstructed columns

sub_graphs.title: DAS Core: Trust Boundaries and Data Integrity
sub_graphs.description: Models security boundaries where external data enters the DAS system and the validation checks applied

nodes.label: DataColumnSidecar Received from Network
nodes.description: A DataColumnSidecar message has been received from the P2P gossip or Req/Resp layer (untrusted input)

nodes.label: Validate Sidecar Format and Index
nodes.description: Check that column index is within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), cell count matches, and sidecar structure is well-formed

nodes.label: Verify Commitment Inclusion Proof
nodes.description: Verify the commitment_inclusion_proof in the sidecar against the signed block header to confirm KZG commitments are part of the canonical block

nodes.label: Verify Cell KZG Proofs
nodes.description: Verify each cell's KZG proof against the corresponding KZG commitment to ensure data integrity

nodes.label: DataColumnSidecar Validated
nodes.description: Sidecar has passed all validation checks: format, inclusion proof, and KZG proofs

nodes.label: DataColumnSidecar Rejected
nodes.description: Sidecar failed validation and is discarded; peer may be penalized

nodes.label: Verify Peer ENR Custody Claim
nodes.description: Verify that a peer claiming higher custody_group_count in their ENR actually serves the corresponding columns

external_entities.name: P2P Network Layer
external_entities.description: Untrusted network peers sending DataColumnSidecars via gossip or Req/Resp; all data must be validated before acceptance

ambiguities.text: Nodes 'SHOULD' reconstruct via recover_matrix when 50%+ columns are obtained - the use of SHOULD (not MUST) leaves reconstruction optional.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume reconstruction is performed by all honest nodes when the threshold is met, since not reconstructing reduces data availability guarantees. This is an assumption that could affect security analysis.

ambiguities.text: The spec does not define the exact timing or deadline for sampling within a slot - when sampling must complete relative to slot boundaries is unspecified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume sampling must complete before the node makes an attestation for the slot. This is an assumption based on the purpose of DAS.

ambiguities.text: custody_group_count can be advertised higher via ENR for 'super-full operation' but the spec does not define penalties for false claims.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume peers can detect false custody claims by requesting columns the peer claims to custody, and may disconnect or penalize non-responsive peers. This needs verification against networking specs.

ambiguities.text: 'Reconstructed columns must be exposed as received network data' - the mechanism for exposing reconstructed data as if received from the network is not defined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the implementation treats reconstructed columns identically to gossip-received columns in its internal data store, making them available to the same query interfaces.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot forge valid KZG proofs for cells without possessing the actual blob data corresponding to the commitments.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker could create fake DataColumnSidecars that pass validation, causing nodes to believe data is available when it is not, breaking data availability guarantees.

implicit_assumptions.description: At least 50% of columns for any given block will be available on the network from honest nodes, ensuring reconstruction is possible.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If fewer than 50% of columns are available, no node can reconstruct the full matrix, and data availability cannot be confirmed despite individual sampling succeeding.

implicit_assumptions.description: The deterministic custody assignment function (get_custody_groups) produces a sufficiently uniform distribution of custody across the network.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If custody assignment is skewed, some columns may have very few custodians, creating data availability holes that an attacker could exploit by targeting few nodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes remain subscribed to their custody group subnets continuously and respond to Req/Resp requests promptly.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If nodes frequently disconnect from subnets or are slow to respond, sampling success rates drop and data availability guarantees weaken, especially under adversarial conditions.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot control enough node IDs to dominate custody of specific columns, since node_id-based assignment is assumed to resist Sybil attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A Sybil attacker could claim custody over targeted columns while withholding data, making those columns unavailable and preventing reconstruction.
